findings.title: Failure threshold can be triggered without enough failed check-ins
findings.body: In try_incident_threshold, when failure_issue_threshold is greater than 1, the code slices the latest check-ins to at most the threshold but never verifies that it actually obtained failure_issue_threshold check-ins. If a monitor with threshold 3 has only one failed check-in, previous_checkins will contain one failure, the OK-check will pass, and the code will set the environment to ERROR and create a MonitorIncident. This creates incidents and issue occurrences before the configured failure threshold is reached. A length check such as returning False when len(previous_checkins) < failure_issue_threshold is needed before changing status or creating the incident.

findings.title: Modified monitor config copy is discarded when building event context
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context copies the monitor config and replaces schedule_type in the local config variable with the human-readable display value, but the returned dictionary uses monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the modified local config. As a result, the prepared schedule_type display value is discarded and the emitted monitor context still contains the raw config value. The returned dict should use the modified config variable.

findings.title: Previous check-in selection is nondeterministic when timestamps tie
findings.body: The query that selects previous check-ins orders only by -date_added. If multiple check-ins have identical date_added values, the subset chosen at the threshold boundary and the selected starting_checkin can be nondeterministic. Adding a tie-breaker such as -id would make the threshold evaluation stable.

findings.title: Occurrences may be created in arbitrary order for threshold check-ins
findings.body: previous_checkins is explicitly reversed into oldest-to-newest order, but the later queryset uses filter(id__in=...) without an order_by. The resulting MonitorCheckIn rows may be returned in arbitrary order, so create_incident_occurrence can be invoked in a different order than the check-ins being represented. If occurrence ordering or detection_time ordering matters, preserve the original ordering when fetching the check-ins.
